## Overview

In week 7, when you learned about shell scripts,
we mentioned that one key goal of this course is to enable you to
submit shell scripts as "batch jobs" at OSC.
This allows you to run them many times simultaneously,
which is extremely useful because with omics data,
it's common to have to run the same step for many samples.

This week, we'll cover the remaining piece in being able to run bioinformatics
tools efficiently at OSC and beyond:
how to submit your shell scripts as batch jobs.

We'll also zoom out to look at the bigger picture:
how do you organize and run your workflows as a whole?

## Learning goals

#### [Slurm batch jobs -- part I](./w10a_slurm1.qmd)

- Different ways to start "compute jobs":
  via OnDemand, with interactive jobs, and with Slurm batch jobs
- How to submit scripts as batch jobs with `sbatch`, and where their output goes
- How to specify `sbatch` options on the command line and inside scripts
- How to monitor and cancel batch jobs with `squeue` and `scancel`

#### [Slurm batch jobs -- part II](./w10b_slurm2.qmd)

- The most common Slurm options, including those to request:
  - More time, cores, and memory for jobs
  - An email notification when jobs e.g. fail or finish
- How to run Slurm jobs in practice, including how to submit many jobs at the same time
- How to make sure that your jobs succeeded
- What to watch out for when using genAI to help with Slurm batch jobs
- How to structure a multi-step workflow,
  and what workflow management systems and nf-core pipelines are
